Global time-scale multiplier for all per-second and per-minute vital rates. Threshold values (BP cutoffs, temperature limits, etc.) are unaffected.

Active playtime, in hours, for a MATU character to complete the transformation. The four growth spurts occur at 25%, 50%, 75% and 100%. Default 168 is one full week of active play. This does not use paceFactor. Changing it also reinterprets the stored progress of existing MATU characters against the new timeline; lowering it may make their next spurt begin immediately.

Multiplier on how fast bleeding drains your blood volume (external + internal). 1.0 = full lethality (hard); 0.75 = a normal setting; 0.5 = easy. Wounds still look the same on the panel - you just bleed out slower on a lower value.

Gameplay balance: multiplier on how strongly covering armor reduces PHYSICAL body wounds after the struck region is known. 1.0 = default balance, 0.5 = half-strength, 0 disables wound reduction. This does not change ballistic stopping, retained-object resistance, insulation, or nonphysical hazards.

Gameplay balance: hard ceiling on the FRACTION of a physical or armor-defeating wound covering armor may remove. Default 0.90 always transmits at least 10% of a wound, even with extreme modded armor. Does not affect a projectile or weak melee hit the armor fully stops before an open wound exists.

Weight of armour ENCHANTMENT protection (Protection, Blast/Projectile/Fire Protection, Feather Falling) against residual body trauma. Uses vanilla's 4% per protection point, then applies this weight and maxArmorWoundReduction. Enchantments never decide whether armor was penetrated. 0 disables this protection.

true = extra MAX HEALTH from RPG/levelling mods toughens the body: incoming sim damage is divided by maxHealth/20, LINEAR rather than diminishing, because diminishing returns get worse the harder a pack scales. Clamped by maxHealthScaleCap, never below 1. Off by default: an easing for packs that are not about hardcore survival.
Ceiling on the max-health divisor above, so a 500-heart pack cannot zero the sim.

true = vanilla/modded HEALING (golden apples, Regeneration, healing spells - anything that fires a heal) reaches the body sim: it clots bleeding wounds (shrapnel still holds them open), closes skin and muscle on the worst limb, and per scope restores blood or chips infection. It NEVER touches brain damage, set fractures or dislocations - those always want real treatment. Off by default: Doomed healing is the point of Doomed.

What the healing bridge may touch. FLESH = clot + skin/muscle. FLESH_AND_BLOOD adds blood restoration. EXTENDED also chips the worst infection slowly - the late-game purge tier, deliberately weak per point of healing.
Multiplier on everything the healing bridge grants per point of healing.

true = healing hearts additively dull pain across the whole body, lightly, so it takes a lot of healing to counteract one broken limb. ~1.5 pain per HP, so a full Regeneration II does NOT clear one broken bone - it is relief, not an analgesic, and it never replaces a splint or a syringe. Independent of vanillaHealingBridge: a pack can want the edge taken off without wanting hearts to close wounds. Off by default.
Multiplier on the pain relief per point of healing above.

Only matters when vanillaHealingBridge is on. false (default) = healing tops your blood up to a normal 5 litres and stops there. true = it keeps pushing past full, toward the 7.5 litre ceiling. Being over-full is not free: it raises blood pressure by up to about a quarter, which brings the hypertensive headache and, sustained, the stroke risk above 180 systolic. Repeated healing - a lifesteal enchantment, say - will get you there on its own. Turn this on if you want that as a hazard to manage rather than something the body simply refuses.

true = calm work pays a little mood: a fish caught, a mature crop harvested. Small and capped per day so a wheat field is not a happiness engine, and routed through the same reward gate as everything else, so a numb body gets less from a good catch.
Total mood a day of fishing and farming can pay, combined. The safe-night sleep gain is 3, so the default 6 makes a full calm day worth two safe nights, never more.

false = a server-policy kill-switch on the entire opioid family, and it now means what it says: they do not appear ANYWHERE. Every administration path is inert and levels already in a body clear out; the items are gone from loot tables, trader shelves, worldgen fluid barrels and every creative tab; wild opium poppies stop generating and a surviving poppy stops dropping anything; and the whole synthesis chain that turns poppies into morphine, heroin and fentanyl is removed from the machines and from JEI/EMI, including the now-irrelevant naloxone chain and supplies. Withdrawal and antagonist decay still run so nobody is left frozen mid-state. Turn this off if opioid use is something your server would rather not simulate at all.

Multiplier on what vanilla potion magic grants the body (the Regeneration blood crumb, Instant Health pain dull and clot nudge). Default 1.0 is the shipped ruling that brewed magic stays tiny; packs that want potions to matter turn it up.
Multiplier on the Regeneration sickness toll (the Witcher price). 0 removes it.

Scale on furniture comfort - the reason bed rest and sitting still are less grueling than standing in a field. Seated on ANY seat mod's chair restores a little stamina - isPassenger is vanilla, so every furniture mod works with zero integration - and sitting near a block in #doomedmatu:comfort_ambience (jukebox, campfire, modded TVs via optional tag entries) trickles mood from the SAME daily budget as fishing and farming. Tiny by design; tweak or zero it here.
Blood volume (litres) you can still function at while bleeding out - the top of the survivable grace window. Default 2.5. Below here you get progressively woozier down to the knockout line.
Hunger. Off = you never get hungry and the Hunger bar is hidden entirely. Use this instead of hungerRateMultiplier=0 if you want another mod to own food.
Thirst. Off = you never get thirsty and the Thirst bar is hidden entirely. Use this instead of thirstRateMultiplier=0 if you want another mod to own drinking.
Stamina and exertion. Off = stamina stays full, the bar is hidden, and nothing in the body sim reads exertion. Use this if another mod owns movement/stamina (Parcool, Epic Fight, etc).

When true, WOUNDS survive death: torn skin, wasted muscle, fractures and their splints carry to the new body. Lethal state never carries - blood, brain, bleeding, infection (including Kuru/prion progression) and organs always reset, so a respawn is never a death loop. Off by default: Doomed's death already costs everything. Turn it on if you want the body you earned to follow you through the respawn.

Micronutrients (iron and six dormant stores). Iron is spent by bleeding and by living, and it gates how fast you rebuild red blood cells - so a transfusion can restore your blood VOLUME and leave your oxygen delivery low. Turn off to make blood loss purely a volume problem.

How much punishment a bone takes before it breaks, as a multiplier on every limb's impact tolerance. 1.0 = default. LOWER breaks bones more easily (0.5 = twice as fragile); higher makes them tougher. Applies to falls and every future impact source.

When true, a head-first landing is lethal outright - the brain is destroyed rather than concussed. Death in this mod is brain death, so this routes through the normal death path, not an instant-kill. Off by default.

When true (default), neurological fumbles can eject the selected stack, offhand stack and next hotbar stack into the world. Set false when a corpse/keep-inventory mod is meant to prevent environmental item loss. Other brain-damage consequences remain active: confused speech, reversed controls, flashes and collapse.

Blood volume (litres) at which you black out (unconscious lockout) and the brain starts its agonal death-drain. Default 1.5. Raise for a harsher, earlier knockout; lower for a longer conscious bleed-out. Held at least 0.25 below graceFunctionalBlood whatever you put here: the two lines are the ends of the consciousness ramp, and closing the gap turns a survivable bleed-out into a one-frame drop.
Multiplier on how fast HUNGER drains. 0.5 = half as fast. Does not affect thirst.
Multiplier on how fast THIRST drains (heat still accelerates it on top).

Multiplier on how FAST core temperature moves toward where the world is dragging it. This is thermal MASS, not severity: it changes how long a change takes, never where you end up. 1.0 is a body that takes a couple of minutes to settle, so you can feel a place turning on you and act before it lands. 7.0 restores the old instant response, where core temperature was effectively a readout of the block you were standing on.

Multiplier on how far the WORLD pulls core temperature away from 37C - biome band, weather, night, altitude and shelter all scale together. 0.5 = a forgiving climate that rarely threatens; 2.0 = a hostile one where exposure kills without gear. Rates are untouched, so a harsher world arrives at its extreme at the same speed.

Maximum block radius used to find nearby fires, ice and Doomed climate machines. The default reaches across a small room. Larger values cost more only during the periodic climate sample, not every game tick.
true (default) = what you eat and drink moves your core temperature: a hot meal warms you, cold water and chilled fruit cool you. false = food is nutrition only.

How much faster thirst ABOVE 100 burns off - drinking past full is wasteful, not free. 1.0 = no waste at all, so a full canteen is worth the same whenever you drink it. The thirst under 100 always drains at its normal rate. Water poisoning past 175 keeps a harder rate on top of this.

true (default) = water scooped straight out of a lake with a glass bottle is as murky as water cupped in your hands, and wants boiling. false = glass bottles sanitise on contact, which is what they used to do: cupping your hands in a pond risked sickness while dipping a bottle in the SAME pond was clean and hydrated you better.
Multiplier on the sickness dirty water gives you. 0 = dirty water is just water, which turns boiling and canteens into flavour. Raise it if your pack wants water to be the thing that kills people.
Multiplier on how fast INFECTION progresses in a wound (and how fast sepsis climbs). 0 = infections never advance. Disinfectant/immunity still work as they do.
Multiplier on the chance that an open wound FIRST becomes infected. This does not alter progression or spread after infection exists. 0 disables spontaneous onset only.
Multiplier on how fast ENERGY drains while awake (exertion, mood and sickness still scale it on top). Sleep recovery is unaffected.
Multiplier on how fast your body REBUILDS blood volume (still needs food). Raise it if bleeding out feels unrecoverable rather than merely brutal.
Multiplier on NATURAL healing - skin and muscle knitting back on their own (sleep and food still scale it on top). Does not affect treatment items.

Multiplier on how much an organ convalesces per in-game day. Recovery is granted at dawn, only for a day in which that organ was not being actively poisoned and the body was fed and rested - it is not a per-second trickle and pace factor does not scale it. An organ can still never be repaired above the permanent loss it has already taken. 0 restores the old behaviour, where organ damage was permanent for life and only a transplant or death undid it.
Multiplier on FRACTURE and DISLOCATION mend timers, separate from soft-tissue healing. 0 prevents bones/joints mending over time; treatment wear still advances normally.
Unrefrigerated blood-bag shelf life in hours at paceFactor 1. The Icebox and powered Freezer slow this clock but never stop it; the server owns all ageing and expiry.

Compatibility bridge for an older documented path. Leave this true and use
features.enableDeepMawSpawns. If an existing server set this false, Doomed transfers
that choice to the canonical feature setting during config load, then resets this alias.
Multiplier on how fast FOOD SPOILS, carried or in a container (biome cold, the Freezer and the Icebox still apply on top). 0 = food never rots.

Optional survival-mod bridges. AUTO selects a single meter/environment owner when the
named mod is present and falls back to Doomed when it is absent or its API is unusable.
DOOMED ignores the external value; EXTERNAL selects it explicitly; INDEPENDENT opts
back into two unrelated simulations and can therefore produce duplicate warnings.

Hydration ownership when Thirst Was Taken (mod id: thirst) is installed.
AUTO/EXTERNAL: its 0-20 meter is canonical; Doomed mirrors it and applies dehydration
to blood, pain and organs without running a second thirst drain.
DOOMED: Doomed is canonical and the external display is mirrored to it each tick.
INDEPENDENT: both meters drain separately. Use only when that duplication is intended.

Thermal ownership when Cold Sweat (mod id: cold_sweat) is installed.
AUTO/EXTERNAL: Cold Sweat supplies WORLD climate and its final insulation-aware RATE;
Doomed remains the core-temperature and medical consequence model.
DOOMED: only Doomed's climate drives its body. INDEPENDENT runs both separately.
Cold Sweat's own HUD and non-damage feedback remain controlled by Cold Sweat.
The bridge never feeds Cold Sweat BODY back into Doomed, avoiding a thermal loop.

When both Create and Thin Air are installed, a worn Create diving helmet plus a
charged backtank can supply air in Thin Air's unbreathable dry environments. Air is
consumed at Create's native one-unit-per-second rate and never twice in one event.
The bridge also prevents event order from erasing Create's normal underwater breath
after its air has already been consumed; lava and unsupported fluids remain unchanged.

Feature toggles gate individual body-sim systems. Most clear or neutralise their own state
when disabled so a paused crisis cannot become permanent; exceptions are stated on the
specific setting. Most default true for the full experience. Settings that ship off say
so on their own lines, and this section also includes a few related modes and limits.
false = the temperature simulation is off: core temperature pins to 37C (movement heat, traps and drugs can no longer push it), and frostbite clears and cannot form.
false = frostbite is off: existing frostbite clears and deep cold no longer freezes limbs, while the wider temperature simulation keeps running.

false = the despair spiral is off: no dread drone, insanity film, or self-harm escalation, and the spiral's state (tier, anhedonia, SSRI course) resets to neutral. Base happiness/mood keep working - they belong to the whole sim, not this system.
false (default) = no flavor chat message for routine medical actions (bandaging, splinting, disinfecting, etc.); the health panel and moodles already show the result. true = restore the narration.

false (default) = players may inject, transfuse or administer mixtures to another player immediately, including while that patient is unconscious. true = the patient must explicitly accept while conscious; an unconscious patient then permits only server-verified emergency injections. This is a server anti-griefing rule, not a client preference. Emergency-equipment access keeps its separate consent rules.

false (default) = non-injection treatments on another player proceed immediately after the server validates the healer, patient, range, anatomy and held tool. true = conscious patients must explicitly accept treatments handled by the co-op treatment gate, including amputation of a limb that could still be saved. Injection consent and emergency-equipment access keep their separate rules.

true (default) = clients may use the one-click medical accessibility option. The server resolves splinting as a fixed competent, non-perfect application; the client cannot claim its own quality. false = all splint procedures must be performed manually.

true = when a player types doom in chat, a DOOMED card slams onto every Doomed player's screen with a fanfare. It is a gag and it is on by default. Turn it off on a public server: anyone can type the word, so anyone can put a banner across everyone else's view. Each player can also switch it off for themselves in the client settings; this is the switch they cannot ignore.

Which run a NEW Doomed character starts on.
  DEFAULT - the health system, indefinitely. No growth spurts, no transformation, no
            Refusal Sequence, no Corebound. You survive the body until it beats you.
  MATU    - the finite run. The transformation advances and the story ends. This is the
            only mode that can unlock the Corebound subclass in the RPG-classes mod,
            because that unlock fires when the transformation completes.
This is the ARC, not the ART - body sprites are a separate per-player cosmetic choice in
the Customization panel, so either mode can wear any body. Existing characters are never
changed by this: anyone already transforming stays on MATU. Players can switch their own
with /doom mode.
ONE OVERRIDE, and it is worth knowing about: with the Fantastic RPG System
(ffrpg) installed, a value of DEFAULT is read as MATU instead, because DEFAULT
can never finish the transformation and so can never unlock the Corebound
subclass that mod waits for. It applies wherever a character is given a run
without being asked, so on an ffrpg pack this line reading DEFAULT does not mean
players get DEFAULT. Set MATU explicitly if that is what you want.

true = a new Doomed character is asked which run they want, once, before the ritual.
false = they silently get defaultMode, for modpacks that have already decided.
The prompt still appears when the ritual intro is skipped: skipping a cutscene should
not quietly pick your run for you.

What happens when a player who is NOT yet Doomed spawns into a world. Standalone
Doomed is opt-in by design, so the default is OFF. Set one of the others for a modpack
built around Doomed, so players don't have to type /doomed in every new world.
  OFF    - players opt in themselves with /doomed or the ritual. (default)
  SILENT - the player simply IS Doomed on first join: no cutscene, no prompt, on the
           server's defaultMode. Ignores letPlayersChooseMode (SILENT is the decided path).
  PROMPT - the ritual (and the one-time mode question, if letPlayersChooseMode is on)
           opens automatically on first join, so the player still chooses without typing.
Fires only for a fresh character (never entered), so it triggers once per new world and
never re-doomes someone who used /doom off, nor a finished Corebound player.

false = wound infection is off: existing limb infection and sepsis CLEAR (not freeze - a frozen sepsis is uncurable), dirty wounds never fester, and the disease layer below also stops, since it reads the immunity this system computes.

false = crawlers and spiders never spawn naturally, and generated Cyst groves do not
create their resident Deep Maw. The ordinary creatures remain low-weight cave
spawns; the Maw is one persistent resident per eligible grove, not a random spawn.
Spawn eggs and spawners still work either way, so
turn this off for a modpack that wants Doomed's body system without Doomed's bestiary.

Independent switch for the one persistent Deep Maw spawned by each eligible Cyst
grove. Leave enableCreatureSpawns on to keep the ordinary bestiary while removing this
territorial apex encounter. Commands and
spawn eggs remain available for mapmakers even when this is false.

Who a Deep Maw may hunt on a mixed server. This is server-authoritative gameplay:
  DOOMED_ONLY - only Survival players with an active Doomed run.
  ALL_SURVIVAL - every non-Creative, non-Spectator player in the encounter. (default)
  AGGRESSORS_FOR_NON_DOOMED - active Doomed players, plus ordinary Survival players
      for five minutes after they damage that specific Maw.
Changing this does not alter natural spawn dimensions, encounter rarity or cosmetics.

Horizontal/vertical block radius around the Deep Maw's saved home in which eligible
prey contribute to its territorial encounter. 96 is the default.
The upper bound matches its hard home-pursuit envelope; this never becomes a client
locator and does not change natural spawn rarity or allowed dimensions.

Multiplies the server's requested Deep Maw pursuit speed after its distance, escape
pressure and severed-anchor logic. Collision, support, loaded chunks and exact hull
validation still decide whether a step is legal. 1.0 keeps the default encounter.

Minimum ticks before the Deep Maw may attempt its strictly off-screen cave catch-up.
The same value raises the cooldown between successful relocations; failed searches retry
at half the value but never faster than ten ticks. Visibility and habitat checks remain.

Multiplies Deep Maw direct tissue injury, ordinary attack damage and forced launch
strength. It deliberately does NOT alter cyst-spore exposure, infection probability,
terrain damage, attack timing or recovery windows. 1.0 preserves consequences.

Minimum block separation between naturally spawned living Deep Maws. This is the
encounter's local population cap: a natural spawn is refused while another living Maw
is inside the cube. Commands and spawn eggs remain exempt. 192 preserves the default.

Allows a hunting Deep Maw's weighted route planner to excavate a minimum movement
corridor when doing so is faster than a loaded open-cave detour. Vanilla/Forge carver,
ore-bearing and cave-growth tags feed #doomedmatu:deep_maw_breachable, which datapacks
may extend for modded geology. mobGriefing, Forge LivingDestroyBlockEvent, block
entities and #doomedmatu:deep_maw_breach_immune still override and refuse it.

Hardness ceiling for a block the Deep Maw may breach. Vanilla stone is 1.5, deepslate
is 3, iron blocks are 5, obsidian is 50. A block above this is treated as a wall and forces
the route planner to look elsewhere. This changes gameplay, never cosmetic presentation.

Maximum blocks one Deep Maw may permanently break in a rolling minute. It only damages
the first obstructed cross-section of its chosen route.
Broken blocks are DESTROYED, not dropped. Excavation is not a mining tool, so the
terrain it takes is gone unless a datapack opts a block into
#doomedmatu:deep_maw_breach_drops. Budget accordingly on a building server: this
number is how much world it may permanently remove per minute, not how much it
will hand back.
Lower this for protected building servers; 0 makes terrain effectively impassable.

false = the disease layer stops entirely: named pathogens (Marrow Fever, Rot Lung,
Marrow Worm) clear along with any prion load - kuru read the brain ungated, so it is
cured, not frozen. Acquired immunity is KEPT (it is progress, not residue).
This is the biggest social mechanic in the mod - it is the only one where
one player's neglect can kill everyone else on the server - so it has its own switch.
NOTE: contagion rides the infection substrate (it reads whole-body immunity and the
antibiotic window), so enableInfection=false switches the disease layer off as well.

Scales every person-to-person transmission roll. 1.0 = default. Lower it for a server
that wants disease to exist without plagues sweeping the base; 0.0 stops all spread while
leaving illnesses that are already contracted running their course.

Per-portion Kuru seed risk for legacy or datapack human flesh with no recorded donor/tissue
provenance. Harvested tissue uses its donor and tissue class instead. Cooking never clears
prion provenance. 0 disables only this compatibility fallback, not contaminated tissue.

false = the character-trait build is off. The perk/flaw pick screen is skipped entirely and every trait effect goes neutral, including for a character who already chose some - claws stop mining, fur stops insulating, and every rate multiplier returns to 1. Turning it back on restores whatever that character picked, because the mask itself is never wiped. For servers that want one body for everyone.

false = internal-organ physiology is off. The liver cascade (sustained painkiller / radiation / sepsis -> toxaemia + jaundice -> hepatic encephalopathy) and the kidney cascade (dehydration / radiation / sepsis -> hyperkalaemia -> heart-rhythm collapse) both stop, and every organ RESTORES to whole - potassium and jaundice are read by the heart and the skin ungated, so a frozen kidney would be an untreatable heart attack. Leave on for the full sim.

false = corpse organ harvesting is off: violent deaths stop scattering the cadaver torso and the bone-saw extraction refuses. The surgeon discipline (INT-gated, freshness-clocked, donor-capped, witnessed, one harvest per donor per 30 min) is grim by design - servers that want transplants to stay loot-only turn this off. Requires enableOrgans. Note: skillsResetOnDeath=true (the default) is ALSO load-bearing here - it is what stops a lone surgeon farming their own respawned corpses, since dying costs them the INT the saw demands.

true = a running antibiotic course actively drives infection back down on every infected limb (about -4%/min net, so a 10-minute oral course knocks roughly 40% off and a bad infection takes two). This is the realistic behaviour: antibiotics kill the bacteria rather than only helping you cope. It stays SLOWER than a topical antiseptic on the wound itself, so source control still matters. false = the old model where antibiotics only raised immunity and could essentially never reverse an infection.
false = radiation is off: no dose accrual, no limb/brain/blood damage, and any existing radiation sickness clears - frozen, it would be a permanent untreatable debuff.
false = contact traps (spike trap, bear trap, sawblade, caltrops, gunmine, coil, sound cannon, grabber plant) inflict no body-sim wounds - they still trigger visually.
true = skip the Matu boss fight and open the old four-wire landmine defusal panel immediately. false (default) = beat Matu first, then complete the wire defusal.

false (default) = llama spit cannot create tissue damage, deep wounds or retained fragments. It can only contaminate an exposed, undressed wound on the struck region. true = llama spit uses the full projectile wound path, including fragments and catastrophic wounds when those systems are enabled.

true = an EXTREME unarmored hit (a .50 BMG-class round or comparably destructive force) GIBS the struck region: a bare head or torso is instant death (the body comes apart), a bare arm/leg is torn off (survivable, but the stump bleeds hard). Ordinary rounds (pistols, SMGs, rifles, arrows) never trigger it. false = those hits wound normally.
false = the Nether-ash lung mechanic stops ticking: breathing the Nether's ash without a dust mask or rebreather no longer builds up in your lungs (existing ash is kept).

true (default) = your Strength/Resilience/Intelligence skill levels reset to baseline when you die, so death costs your training. false = skills persist across death (the old behaviour). Does NOT apply to /doomedheal.

true (default) = the once-per-life LAST STAND second wind can fire at the brink - the 'I won't give up yet' cutscene that sometimes pulls you back from brain death. false = no last stand and no cutscene; the brink is final. Turn off if you don't want the reprieve, or if the cutscene conflicts with another mod's death/voice handling.

false = chemistry-machine fumes no longer harm you: standing near a running kiln/still/reactor without a mask stops causing sickness/nausea/toxic chest injury. The machines still run and the other hazards (fire, overheat, explosions) are unaffected.
true = carried food slowly spoils over time and is eventually lost. false = food never spoils.
true = blood bags age and eventually become unsafe to transfuse. false = their stored condition remains fresh; food spoilage is a separate switch.

true = Strength limits main-inventory slots. The hotbar always works. At Strength 0, 3 main slots are usable. More open as Strength rises. false = all slots work. Disable this for inventory layout mods.
true = usable slots start at the top left. false = they start at the bottom right.

EXPERIMENTAL (default off): true = every carried item, including VANILLA ones, adds weight, so a heavy inventory encumbers you (slower movement, faster stamina drain). Doomed items already have weights; this extends weight to vanilla items. Off while it is being balanced - turn it on to try it and report how it feels.
EXPERIMENTAL fallback mass in kg PER ITEM for vanilla/modded stacks that have no assigned Doomed ItemInfo weight. 0 disables only this fallback, Doomed item weights stay.

true = your vanilla HEALTH BAR is driven by your overall condition (brain / blood) so external health-bar HUD mods show something meaningful instead of always-full. The bar never reaches 0 - real death is still brain-death only, the mod keeps owning when you actually die. On by default so health-bar mods work out of the box. false = Doomed stops using hearts as a condition display. Ordinary damage may still dent the vanilla bar, especially while starving with Doomed hunger disabled, but cannot cause Doomed death.

Player appearance customization - the Customization hub opened by the canvas icon on the
status panel. Every allow* switch defaults true (players may customize). A modpack that has
decided its intended look sets the forced* value(s) below AND flips the matching allow* to
false: players then get exactly that look and cannot change it. This is a HARD lock - the
server value is what actually renders, so a player cannot bypass it by hand-editing their
own client config. When an option is unlocked (allow*=true), its forced* value is ignored
and the player's own choice applies. All SERVER-side, so the whole thing holds in multiplayer.

Master switch. false = the whole Customization hub is locked: every option below is
disabled regardless of its own switch, and each renders its forced* value. true = the
per-option switches below apply individually.

false = players cannot change the interface accent colour or theme; forcedAccentColor +
forcedTheme render instead.
The accent colour (packed 0xRRGGBB) every player gets when allowInterfaceStyle is false.
The interface theme every player gets when allowInterfaceStyle is false.
false = players cannot change the status-panel body sprites; forcedBodyStyle renders instead.

The body sprite set (DOOMED=Matu / HUMAN / ALT=Furry) every player gets when allowBodyStyle
is false. A style with no art installed still falls back to the shipped doll.
false = players cannot toggle Hide Transformation Model; forcedHideTransformModel applies.
Whether the grown horns/tail are hidden when allowTransformModelToggle is false.

false = players cannot toggle Show Vanilla Hearts; forcedShowVanillaHearts applies. (The
hearts also still require the server's mirrorHealthToVanilla to actually show.)
Whether the vanilla hearts show when allowVanillaHearts is false.

false = force the optional hunger/thirst hotbar icon rows hidden for every player and lock
their Customization toggle. This is presentation only: hunger, thirst, their moodles and
all gameplay continue unchanged. true = each player may choose locally; their default is hidden.
false = players cannot choose Celsius/Fahrenheit display; forcedTemperatureUnit applies. This is presentation only: the simulation always remains Celsius.
Temperature display unit every player gets when allowTemperatureUnit is false.
false = players cannot move, scale or re-anchor the moodle HUD; the forced Moodle values below render instead. This changes presentation only, never which moodles exist.
Moodle scale every player gets when allowMoodleHudLayout is false. Critical warnings still enforce the client renderer's 0.75 readability floor.
Moodle screen corner every player gets when allowMoodleHudLayout is false.
Forced horizontal moodle offset in virtual HUD pixels; final placement is screen-clamped.
Forced vertical moodle offset in virtual HUD pixels; final placement is screen-clamped.

false = players cannot open the Fit Puppet Art editor; the shipped puppet proportions apply
(any saved per-limb fit is ignored while locked).

false = players cannot edit their character dialogue or switch the resource-pack dialogue
source. Server-authoritative: a locked server resets custom/resource lines to the built-in
dialogue, because quips broadcast over your head for everyone to see.

false = players cannot choose the public colour or overhead-bubble state of their chat; forcedChatColor and forcedOverheadChat apply. Dialogue voice/pitch stay cosmetic but are validated and shared so nearby listeners hear the speaker's chosen voice; the optional physical-key feedback itself remains local and is never server-locked.
Public chat-text colour (packed 0xRRGGBB) used when allowChatPresentation is false.

Bookkeeping rather than a setting: it records that the one-time presentation defaults have already been applied to this server. Leave it alone. Setting it back to 0 lets the mod overwrite a forced chat colour you deliberately set to pure white the next time the world loads.
Whether ordinary chat appears over the speaker when allowChatPresentation is false.

MASTER switch. false = NOTHING Doomed generates in newly generated chunks - no grabber plants, traps, mines, drop capsules, trader lairs, cyst jungle, cave flora, ferns or herbs. For running Doomed alongside other worldgen-heavy mods without its features. Chunks that already generated are unaffected. Leave true and use the per-feature toggles below for finer control.

false = hazard TRAPS (spike/bear traps, mines, live wires, sound cannons, grabber plants...) no longer generate in NEWLY generated chunks. Traps already in your world stay, and beneficial scatter (crates, plants, resources) is unaffected.
Multiplier on how many traps generate per chunk. 1.0 = default, 0.0 = none, 2.0 = twice as many. Capped by the per-chunk attempt count, so very high values plateau.

Chance per eligible underground cave-floor attempt to TRY a drop capsule in NEW chunks. The capsule still needs a dry, roomy, chunk-safe crash site, so the observed rate is much lower. Default 0.16 makes capsules findable without making them common; set 0.04 for the legacy rarity or 0.0 to disable their natural generation.

true (default) = sparse GLOWCAP survival flora generates on cave floors - a renewable food + bandage source underground so caving isn't a dead end. It glows faintly. Set false if you don't want any glowy plants in your caves.
Multiplier on how much cave flora generates. 1.0 = default (deliberately SPARSE), 0.0 = none, 3.0 = lush. Kept low so it never floods your caves with glow.

Maximum MATURE cultivated bittermoss within five horizontal blocks. Younger cuttings remain alive but stop at age 1 while the patch is full. Default 4 keeps the renewable early antiseptic useful without turning one cold cellar into industrial medicine.

Generate the Deep Maw's bounded underground cyst jungle in newly generated chunks. The biome uses dense pass-through flora, hanging vines, shallow lakes and rare clean-water pod plants; it never spreads into arbitrary player blocks after generation.

Broad cyst-jungle rarity. The world is divided into deterministic 8x8-chunk underground regions; one region in this many is selected. 1 makes every eligible region cyst growth, 16 is the rare default, and 128 is extremely rare. Forge keeps whatever value an existing world's server config already saved, so a world made under an earlier version keeps its old rarity until you set this one by hand.

true (default) = cyst territory runs its bounded biological lifecycle: exposed larvae, interruptible dormant corpses, motile carriers and finite rooted brood nodes. false keeps the complete biome palette and water pods but removes this hostile ecology.

true (default) = cyst eyes sweep their spotlights, are pulled toward a carried light, and report a player they catch to nearby Deep Maws. false leaves them standing as inert scenery - they stop sweeping, stop lighting the cave and stop telling anything where you are.

true (default) = each generated cyst grove remembers server-confirmed disturbance. Being seen, heard, breaking tissue, shooting lenses, mining and starting nearby fires raise a hidden shared value that only speeds the eyes' ordinary sweep. It never widens their cone, bypasses cover, changes calm green beams to yellow, or directly alerts a Maw.
Minutes with no living survival player inside the underground grove for maximum agitation to settle back to calm. Presence freezes decay but does not raise agitation by itself.

true (default) = prolonged breathing near cyst spore blooms builds a hidden, recoverable particulate burden. Respiratory protection slows it sharply; only sustained unprotected exposure can seed the existing treatable Marrow Worm pathway. This is gameplay-only and independent of the client's spore/fog visual settings.

Multiplier on how quickly cyst-spore burden accumulates. 1.0 is the intended slow burn; 0.0 disables new burden while keeping every cyst visual and structure, and values above 1.0 make unprotected biome expeditions medically harsher.

Free trait points every new character starts with. 0 (default) is the shipped rule: the budget starts empty, so every perk has to be paid for by agreeing to be worse at something else. Raise it for a softer run where a perk or two is free; a negative value starts people in debt, owing flaws before they can play.

true (default) = one player can amputate another. A limb that is already lost (necrotic, gangrenous or destroyed) can be taken from someone who cannot answer, because that is the emergency the feature exists for. A limb that could still be saved asks first only when requireCrossPlayerTreatmentConsent is enabled. false removes the cross-player amputation interaction entirely.

Maximum combined cyst carriers and dispersal larvae within 32 blocks. Rooted nodes wait rather than spawning past this limit. This is the anti-exponential population budget; raising it makes loaded cyst jungles substantially more hostile.

false (default) = player deaths never create a colonized corpse carrier. true opts the server into a separate hostile carrier entity after a player dies on cyst substrate; it never takes ownership of, deletes or modifies another mod's protected player corpse.

true (default) = grabber plants (the 'snake grabbers' that seize and thrash you) generate on the surface in new chunks. false = none generate - independent of the trap toggle, so you can keep the mines/traps and lose only the grabbers, or vice versa.
Multiplier on grabber-plant spawn rate. 1.0 = default, 0.0 = none, 2.0 = twice as many. Lower this if grabbers feel too common.

false (default) = grabber plants only ever seize PLAYERS. true = they also seize creatures that wander into reach, thrash them and throw them clear, exactly as they do to you. Bosses are NEVER grabbed whatever you put here - a plant is not going to pick up the wither - and neither are other grabber plants' victims, tamed pets, or anything too big to lift. Narrow it further with grabberMobWhitelist below.

Which creatures a plant may seize, when grabberGrabsMobs is true. EMPTY (default) = any hostile monster. Otherwise ONLY the entity ids listed here, hostile or not - e.g. ["minecraft:zombie", "minecraft:skeleton"] for a plant that eats the shambling ones and ignores everything else. Ids are "modid:entity"; unknown ids are ignored rather than crashing, so a list can outlive the mod that needed it.
true (default) = trader lair structures (the maid / adventurer vendor rooms) generate underground in new chunks. false = they no longer generate.

ATTEMPT rarity for trader lairs in eligible newly generated chunks. 24 (default) =
the feature attempts a site on average once per 24 eligible calls; 1 = every eligible
call. This is not a promise of one completed lair per N chunks: the buried footprint,
dryness, clearance, template, biome tag, and dimension policy may still reject it.
Existing chunks are unaffected. Use enableTraderLairs=false to disable them entirely.

How many ORDINARY items you may sell to traders inside one window. 5 (default). The
throttle exists so a player cannot dump a mountain of cheap junk to bank credit for the
expensive stock; it is counted per PLAYER across every trader, so shop-hopping does not
reset it. Raise it if scavenging feels punished rather than paced.

The higher cap for crafted MEDICINE, so growing and brewing to sell stays viable. 10
(default). The two share one count, so this is really the total: at most this many items
per window, of which at most traderSellCap may be non-medical. Set below traderSellCap and
medicine simply gets no bonus.

Length of the rolling sell window, in REAL minutes. 60 (default).
THIS IS REAL TIME, NOT GAME TIME - it is wall-clock, so a fast-daylight server or a slept
night does not advance it, and one window is about 72 in-game hours at default daylength.
The distinction matters on servers with altered day length, so it is stated here plainly.
Set 0 to remove the throttle entirely. The window is in memory only and resets on a server
restart, which players cannot force.

Most credit you can bank with a single trader at once. 60 (default).
READ THIS BEFORE RAISING IT: the same number is also the ceiling on what traders will
STOCK, so anything worth more than this is excluded from their shelves entirely. At 60
that hides expensive core gear such as titanium prosthetics (180). Content-provider
exclusion lists still win at every cap, so raising this cannot silently expose a weapon
its owning mod marked find-only. Banked credit is clamped down on its next write, so
lowering it is safe.

Base game ticks between shelf replenishments at an average shelter. 48000 (default), about
two Minecraft days. A failing shelter waits 1.5x this and an established one 0.5x, so the
condition system still means something, and a jitter is applied on top. Pair this with
traderSellWindowMinutes: if credit takes an hour to earn AND the shelf takes days to
refill, the two waits stack and the shop reads as a one-time loot pinata.

How many sold lots come back per replenishment at an average shelter. 2 (default); a
failing shelter restores one fewer and an established one one more. Restoring more lots
than were actually sold is harmless - it is bounded by what is missing.

Actual-dimension policy for all Doomed generated content. Biome eligibility remains a
separate datapack gate through #doomedmatu:worldgen_biomes; BOTH must allow a site.
OVERWORLD_ONLY = only minecraft:overworld (default).
ALLOW_LIST = only IDs in worldgenDimensionIds.
ALL_EXCEPT_DENY_LIST = every dimension except IDs in worldgenDimensionIds.

Dimension IDs used by worldgenPolicy, e.g. ["minecraft:overworld",
"examplemod:underground"]. Unknown but well-formed IDs remain valid for optional mods;
malformed IDs are ignored. This never adds a dimension's biomes to the worldgen tag.
Worth knowing if you are writing a datapack: the BIOME half of the policy comes from a
per-position filter that the scatter and trader-lair features carry and the two CYST
features do not. A grove is a multi-chunk carved cavern and filtering it per position
would punch holes in it at tag boundaries. So for cyst groves this is a DIMENSION
filter only, and the biome tag does not narrow it further.

Independent actual-dimension policy for NATURAL crawler, spider and Deep Maw spawns,
and for the cyst lifecycle's own carriers and brood larvae.
Read it as a VETO rather than a permit. The crawler and the spider genuinely spawn on
their own and this decides where. The Deep Maw does not - it is spawned by generated
groves, so allowing a dimension here cannot put one anywhere worldgenPolicy has not
already placed a grove. It can only take away.
Biome eligibility still requires #doomedmatu:creature_spawn_biomes. Spawners, commands,
and spawn eggs remain available.
OVERWORLD_ONLY = only minecraft:overworld (default).
ALLOW_LIST = only IDs in creatureSpawnDimensionIds.
ALL_EXCEPT_DENY_LIST = every dimension except IDs in creatureSpawnDimensionIds.

Dimension IDs used by creatureSpawnPolicy. This list is intentionally separate from
worldgenDimensionIds so enabling resources never silently enables hostile encounters.
Unknown but well-formed IDs remain valid; malformed IDs are ignored.

Hours a player must stay continuously ALIVE (per life, reset on death) before the WITNESS tablet HACK becomes possible - IRIS decrypting the Bureau uplink. Default 12. 0 = available immediately; 2160 = 90 real days.

Partial-save the alive-timer on death. 0 (default) = the timer FULLY resets to 0 when you die - the intended hardcore behaviour. N > 0 = instead it drops to the last completed N-hour checkpoint, so a death costs at most N hours (e.g. 1 = saves every hour: die at 6h30 -> back to 6h). The hack stays permanent once earned either way.

Locked crate loot for a DOOMED player who lockpicks it - ONE entry dropped at weighted random. Each entry is "modid:item [count] [weight]" (count + weight optional, default 1; higher weight = more common). ALL FOUR rosters also accept "@table modid:path [weight]" to roll a datapack loot table when the pick lands on it - one line splices in a whole custom table, no hand-porting. Core defaults to the full medical roster: consumables are common (weight 3), potent drugs uncommon (2), durable tools like the defibrillator/bone saw rare (1). Required content companions merge their own configurable entries at runtime without putting their item IDs in this core config. Modpack devs: edit freely.
Locked crate loot for a NON-Doomed (vanilla) player who pries one open - ONE entry dropped at random. Mundane valuables only, and never diamonds.

Sealed pod (keypad) loot - TWO entries, always different items, dropped when it opens. Same format and same full medical roster as lockedCrateLoot (consumables common, durable tools rare). Modpack devs: edit freely - e.g. trim this to just the rarer drugs for a high-value stash.

Drop-capsule loot - a cracked capsule spills 3-5 DISTINCT entries at random. How cleanly you opened it does not change the count. Rich CONSUMABLES (meds/drugs/food + a few valuables), NO permanent gear so it never shortcuts the tech tree. "id [count] [weight]". Modpack devs: edit freely.

Seconds on the deceptive "LOCKOUT" clock once a drop capsule is torn open, before it detonates. The label reads like a harmless re-seal timer but it is lethal. Default 180: a calm clean open survives; only greed or fumbling kills. Lower = a tighter race.

Set this to 2 once you have read the startup warning that lists shipped loot entries missing from your edited lists. That silences the warning for this release. The mod never inserts or rewrites loot you have customized, and a later release may raise the number and warn once more.

Internal schema marker written into core configs created after content-provider policy was split into companion-owned files. Do not lower it: companions use its pre-correction presence to preserve older administrator choices instead of inserting new content.
Internal crash-recovery journal for provider config migrations. Entries are generic provider IDs, not gameplay settings. They clear only after the destination file saves.
Opaque value snapshots paired with the provider migration journal. This preserves old administrator choices if Forge saves its correction before a companion can commit.
